issues.legal_issue: The statutory delegation of power to Commissioners of Divisions to exercise specified governmental functions is constitutionally valid where the legislature has laid down the policy and left administrative reorganisation to the executive.
material_facts: A state statute authorised the government to confer statutory powers and duties on Commissioners of Divisions by notification and to make corresponding adaptations to enactments.
The land acquisition proceedings relied on powers conferred on Commissioners under that statutory arrangement.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the validity of the Commissioners of Divisions Act on grounds of excessive delegation and legislative abdication failed.
issues.legal_principle: Following Arnold Rodricks & Anr. v. State of Maharashtra & Ors., [1966] 3 S.C.R. 885, the delegation was guided by the legislature's policy of reorganising administration consequent on the establishment of Commissioners of Divisions and did not amount to abdication of legislative power.

predicates.delegation_validity_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a law that delegates statutory functions to administrative officers.
predicates.legislature_set_policy: The legislature stated the policy guiding the delegation.
predicates.executive_role_limited_to_administrative: The executive was authorised to organise administration in accordance with that legislative policy.

issues.definition: When a delegation-validity challenge concerns a delegation guided by legislative policy and limited to administrative reorganisation, the delegation is valid.

issues.legal_issue: A competent successor authority may issue a final land-acquisition declaration following a valid preliminary notification issued by a competent authority before a territorial reorganisation, without issuing a new preliminary notification.
material_facts: The preliminary notification was issued by the Commissioner who was competent in the then-existing state.
After the state was reorganised, the relevant area became part of a new state.
The Commissioner competent in the new state issued the final declaration under the continuing statutory arrangement.
issues.conclusion: The successor Commissioner's final declaration was valid, and a fresh preliminary notification from that Commissioner was not required.
issues.legal_principle: The Land Acquisition Act and the Commissioners of Divisions Act did not require the authority issuing the final declaration to issue a fresh preliminary notification where the earlier notification had been issued by a competent authority and the successor authority was competent to issue the declaration.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of land-acquisition notifications.
predicates.preliminary_notice_issued_by_competent_a: An authority competent at the time issued the preliminary notification.
predicates.territorial_reorganisation_occurred: A territorial reorganisation occurred between the preliminary notification and the final declaration.
predicates.successor_authority_competent_for_final_: The authority in the reorganised territory was competent to issue the final declaration.

issues.definition: Where a competent authority issued the preliminary notice and a competent successor authority issues the final declaration after territorial reorganisation, no fresh preliminary notice is required.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality need not first attempt to purchase land by agreement before seeking its acquisition through the government.
material_facts: The municipal corporation resolved to move the government to acquire the land.
The challenge asserted that an attempt to acquire the land by agreement had to precede the government's acquisition proceedings.
issues.conclusion: A prior attempt to acquire the land by agreement was not a condition for moving the government to acquire it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 77(1) and 78(1) of the Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 provide alternative means of acquisition; the opening words of section 78(1) do not make an unsuccessful agreement under section 77 a prerequisite to an application to the government.

predicates.municipal_acquisition_request: A municipal authority sought government acquisition of land for a municipal undertaking.
predicates.agreement_purchase_not_attempted: The municipal authority had not first attempted to purchase the land by agreement.

issues.definition: When a municipal authority seeks government acquisition, the absence of a prior attempted agreement does not prevent that request.

issues.legal_issue: Land acquisition for a memorial to a nationally venerated figure at a place associated with that figure is for a public purpose even if the purpose is not established as a municipal purpose.
material_facts: The land was sought for a memorial to Mahatma Gandhi at a place associated with him.
The notices identified the memorial as the purpose of acquisition.
The Court regarded Mahatma Gandhi as being held in universal veneration in the country.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was for a public purpose in the ordinary sense, so it was unnecessary to rely on the extended statutory meaning of public purpose or to decide whether the memorial was a municipal purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The ordinary meaning of public purpose in section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 covered acquisition for this memorial; the extended meaning in section 78(1) of the Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 was therefore unnecessary to the decision.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges a land-acquisition notification.
predicates.memorial_for_nationally_venerated_figure: The land was sought for a memorial to a figure widely venerated in the country.
predicates.site_associated_with_figure: The proposed memorial site was associated with that figure.

issues.definition: In a challenge to an acquisition for a memorial, a site associated with a widely venerated figure makes the acquisition a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: The legality of a municipality's use of its funds after land has been acquired for a public purpose is outside the inquiry into the validity of that acquisition.
material_facts: The land was being acquired for a purpose the Court found to be a public purpose.
The appellants argued that municipal funds would be unlawfully used to establish the memorial after acquisition.
issues.conclusion: Whether municipal funds could lawfully be used for the memorial was not a matter within the inquiry in this appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Once the land is being acquired for a public purpose, the validity of the acquisition does not require deciding whether a municipality would act within its powers in later using municipal funds for the project.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_purpose_is_public: The purpose for which the land is acquired is a public purpose.
predicates.challenge_concerns_later_municipal_spend: The challenge concerns whether a municipality may lawfully spend its funds on the project after acquisition.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns acquisition for a public purpose but disputes only later municipal spending, the spending issue is outside review of the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: A land-acquisition notification is not invalid merely because it does not identify the instrumentality that will carry out the public purpose.
material_facts: The acquisition notifications identified the public purpose but did not specify the instrumentality that would execute it.
The appellants argued that the omission made the notifications unenforceable.
issues.conclusion: The omission of the executing instrumentality did not affect the validity of either notification.
issues.legal_principle: The Land Acquisition Act does not require the instrumentality carrying out the public purpose to be specified in notifications under sections 4 and 6. The Court approved Ramji Popatbhai v. Jamnadas Shah, (1969) Guj. L.R. 164, and followed Vishnu Prasad Ramdas Gohil & Others v. The State of Gujarat, C.A. No. 1983 of 1966, decided October 9, 1969.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a land-acquisition notification.
predicates.public_purpose_identified: The notification identifies the public purpose for which the land is sought.
predicates.implementing_instrumentality_omitted: The notification does not identify the instrumentality that will carry out the purpose.

issues.definition: If a notification identifies the public purpose but omits the implementing instrumentality, that omission does not invalidate it.

issues.legal_issue: A difference in the areas described in preliminary and final acquisition notifications, accompanied by language excluding land not needed, does not by itself establish that the issuing authority failed to apply its mind.
material_facts: The final declaration described a different area from the preliminary notification, including a larger area from one survey parcel.
The final declaration stated that the remaining area was abandoned or excluded.
The Court considered that wording consistent with excluding the part not needed for the public purpose.
issues.conclusion: There was no justification on these facts for finding that the Commissioner had failed to apply his mind when issuing the final declaration.
issues.legal_principle: The wording and circumstances of the declaration could reasonably be understood as excluding land not needed for the public purpose; the discrepancy did not establish non-application of mind.

rule.if: acquisition_notification_challenge and area_descriptions_differ and final_notice_excludes_unneeded_land and discrepancy_alone_indicates_no_failure_to_consider_materials

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a final land-acquisition declaration.
predicates.area_descriptions_differ: The areas described in the preliminary notice and final declaration differ.
predicates.final_notice_excludes_unneeded_land: The final declaration's wording indicates that land not needed for the purpose is excluded.
predicates.discrepancy_alone_indicates_no_failure_t: The discrepancy, considered with the exclusion wording, does not establish that the authority failed to consider the relevant materials.

issues.definition: A difference in stated areas does not disprove application of mind when the final notice's wording indicates exclusion of land not needed and the discrepancy alone shows no failure to consider relevant materials.
